source.title: Deep Neural Networks With Trainable Activations and Controlled Lipschitz Constant
source.authors: Shayan Aziznejad; Harshit Gupta; Joaquim Campos; M. Unser

record.file_problem: Text is the full paper; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies trainable activations and a Lipschitz regularizer. It reports classification performance, but does not measure the training-to-test gap or test a listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports performance for an area-classification task and test accuracy on MNIST under different activation schemes and spline sizes. These results do not establish whether training error and test error diverge or track one another.
record.test_reason: The study tests learned spline activations and Lipschitz-based regularization, not any listed version. Its width illustrations do not establish zero training error or performance beyond interpolation; its spline-coefficient sweep changes activation complexity rather than network width. It makes no qualifying architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The conclusion chiefly emphasizes the variational framework, a global Lipschitz bound, and existence of a solution with continuous piecewise-linear activations. Numerical illustrations show performance and sparsity benefits. The regularizer controls an upper bound and does not guarantee minimization of the actual Lipschitz constant.
record.recipe_differences: Trains fully connected area classifiers and an MNIST convolutional network with learned activations; does not use the random-label or train-test-gap measurements in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that performance increases with spline coefficient count K until saturation; changing λ affects error rate, the Lipschitz bound, and the number of active ReLUs. The ℓ1 and ℓ2 outer-norm configurations have similar area-classification performance but different sparsity and parameter counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned spline activations outperform the tested standard activations in area classification; increasing spline-coefficient count improves performance until saturation in area classification and MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning more expressive activations with Lipschitz-based regularization can improve classification performance in small architectures.

record.problems: The reported area-classification performance metric is not defined as test performance in the supplied text. MNIST accuracy values are shown only in a figure, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The experiments do not report a train-test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test-error behavior as network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that mitigate them.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparative ranking of measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The lack of a train-test-gap measurement alone does not exclude testing all versions; the decisive issue is the absence of their specified comparisons. Figure 5 labels both area-classification and MNIST performance as test accuracy, although Table I does not explicitly identify its evaluation split. A Lipschitz bound on input-output sensitivity is not V7's magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same training recipe.
Test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD on held-out performance.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
